mainTopic: Searching for a truly 'difficult' ruling in money law: a grandson undoing his father's sale, and witnesses who become unfit after signing
overview: The גמרא is searching for a ruling that truly deserves the label 'difficult in money law.' It first quotes a ruling: a son sold his father's property during the father's lifetime and then died, and the grandson takes the property back from the buyers. It answers that the grandson inherits straight from his grandfather, based on the פסוק 'תחת אבותיך יהיו בניך.' It then tries a בכור who sold his חלק בכורה, and answers that the grandson stands in his father's place. Next it tries three witness cases: a witness who later became a גזלן, one who later inherited the field, and one who later became the חתן. In each case he cannot confirm his own signature, but others can. The first two are pushed off by saying the signature was already confirmed in בית דין. The חתן case is pushed off because relatives are disqualified by a גזירת מלך, as shown from משה and אהרן. So the גמרא returns to the first case and says the פסוק is only a blessing. It then begins to question that reading, and the challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The grandson takes back land his father sold
steps.stepSummary: A ruling is quoted: if a son sold his father's property during the father's lifetime and then died, the grandson can take the property back from the buyers. This was called a 'difficult' ruling in money law.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: A son sold some of his father's property while his father was still alive, and then the son died. The son's son takes the property back from the buyers. And this is a difficult ruling in money law. The buyers can say to him: Your father sold it, and you take it back?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ruling about a grandson who takes back land his father sold. It also quotes the complaint that this ruling seems unfair to the buyers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son sold land that was not yet his, because his father was still alive. Once the son dies, the grandson takes the land back. The buyers complain that it is strange for a son to undo his own father's sale.

keyTerms.meaning: Takes back from the hands of

phrases.english: It was stated: A son who sold some of his father's property
during his father's lifetime, and he died –
phrases.notes: The one who died here is the son who made the sale.

phrases.english: his son takes it back from the buyers.
And this is a difficult ruling in money law –
for the buyers can say to him:
Your father sells, and you take it back?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: בֵּן שֶׁמָּכַר בְּנִכְסֵי אָבִיו בְּחַיֵּי אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion with a quoted ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A grandson takes back from the buyers land that his father sold during the grandfather's lifetime, and this ruling is called 'difficult'.

steps.title: No difficulty: the grandson inherits straight from the grandfather
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the ruling is not hard at all. The grandson can claim that he inherits directly from his grandfather, and a פסוק supports this.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the difficulty? Maybe he can say: I come on the strength of my father's father. Know that this is true, as it is written: 'In place of your fathers will be your sons; you will make them princes in all the land.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the claim that the ruling is difficult. The grandson is not undoing his father's sale, because he inherits from the grandfather himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyers' complaint only works if the grandson inherits through his father. If he inherits directly from his grandfather, his father's sale never touches what the grandson receives. The פסוק 'in place of your fathers will be your sons' is the support for this.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the difficulty? (the problem is being dismissed)
I come on the strength of my father's father
Know (that this is so), introducing a support

steps.whyThisMatters: This idea, that a grandson inherits straight from the grandfather, drives the next steps. Step 14 later undercuts its source by reading the פסוק as only a blessing.

phrases.english: And what is the difficulty?
Perhaps he can say:
I come on the strength of my father's father –
Know that this is so, as it is written:
"In place of your fathers will be your sons,
you will make them princes in all the land"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the claim from Step 1 that the ruling is difficult.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The label 'difficult' given to the ruling in Step 1.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The complaint assumes the grandson inherits through his father. In fact he inherits directly from the grandfather, so his father's sale does not bind him.

steps.title: A harder case: a firstborn who sold his extra share
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a better example of a difficult ruling: a בכור sold his חלק בכורה during his father's life and died before his father. His son still takes it back from the buyers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if anything is difficult, this is difficult: A firstborn son sold his firstborn share during his father's lifetime, and he died during his father's lifetime. His son takes it back from the buyers. And this is a difficult ruling in money law: his father sells, and he takes it back?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new case that it thinks truly deserves the label 'difficult'. It is setting up the next step, which explains why this case is harder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case is like the first one, but the land sold is the extra חלק בכורה. That extra share belongs only to a בכור, and that detail is what makes this case seem harder.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, if anything is difficult, this is difficult

phrases.english: Rather, if anything is difficult, this is difficult –
a firstborn son who sold the firstborn's share
during his father's lifetime, and died during his father's lifetime –
his son takes it back from the buyers.
And this is a difficult ruling in money law –
his father sells, and he takes it back?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 2 removed the difficulty from the first case, this step offers a different case as the truly difficult one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A grandson takes back the חלק בכורה that his firstborn father sold, even though his father died before the grandfather.

steps.title: The grandfather argument seems not to work here
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks the earlier answer. If the grandson comes through his grandfather, why should he get the בכור share? Only his father was the grandfather's בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say that here too he says: I come on the strength of my father's father. But if he comes on the strength of his father's father, what does he have to do with the firstborn's share?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא expects someone to repeat the answer from Step 2, and explains why it seems not to fit this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Toward his grandfather, the grandson is a grandson, not a בכור. The only link he has to the בכור share is through his father. So it looks like he must be coming through his father, and then his father's sale should bind him.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (expecting an answer)
What does he have to do with it?

phrases.english: And if you will say that here too he says:
I come on the strength of my father's father;

phrases.aramaic: אִי מִכֹּחַ אֲבוּהּ דְּאַבָּא קָא אָתְיָא,
phrases.english: if he comes on the strength of his father's father,
what does he have to do with the firstborn's share?
phrases.notes: He is not his grandfather's בכור, so the extra share seems to come only through his father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer from Step 2 seems not to fit the new case from Step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Using the 'from my grandfather' answer of Step 2 for the בכור case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The right to a חלק בכורה seems to come only through the father, who was the בכור.

steps.title: No difficulty: he inherits from the grandfather in his father's place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects this case too. The grandson inherits from his grandfather, but he stands in his father's place, so he also gets the בכור share.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the difficulty? Maybe he can say: I come on the strength of my father's father, and I stand in my father's place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the second case is not difficult either. The grandson can get both things: a direct right from the grandfather, and his father's position as בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inheriting from the grandfather means the father's sale does not bind the grandson. Standing in the father's place means he takes the share his father would have taken, including the חלק בכורה. So the question from Step 4 is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: I stand in my father's place

steps.whatToRemember: For now, both cases are answered the same way: the grandson can claim he inherits straight from his grandfather, so his father's sale does not bind him, and he stands in his father's place for the בכור share. Step 14 later reads the פסוק as only a blessing, so the first case becomes difficult again.
steps.confusionAlert: Standing 'in my father's place' does not mean he inherits through his father. It only sets the size of his share; the inheritance itself still comes straight from the grandfather.

phrases.english: And what is the difficulty?
Perhaps he can say:
I come on the strength of my father's father –
and I stand in my father's place!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in Step 4 and removes the difficulty from the case in Step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the בכור case of Step 3 is a difficult ruling.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes that inheriting from the grandfather and taking the father's place cannot go together. In fact the grandson can do both.

steps.title: A witness who later became a robber
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a new candidate for the 'difficult' ruling. A witness signed a שטר, then became a גזלן. He cannot confirm his own handwriting, but others can. How can others be believed when he is not?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if there is a difficult ruling, it is this one: someone signed as a witness on a document before he became a robber, and then he became a robber. He cannot testify that the handwriting is his, but other people can. Now, if he himself is not believed, how can others be believed? This is the ruling that is difficult in money law.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the earlier examples were rejected, the גמרא tries a new example of a ruling that is 'difficult in money law': a witness who became a גזלן after signing a שטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a person becomes a גזלן, he is no longer a valid witness, so he cannot confirm his own signature. Yet others are allowed to say 'this is his handwriting,' and the שטר stands. That seems backwards, because the witness himself knows the truth best, and he is the one being turned away.

keyTerms.meaning: A robber. He becomes unfit to serve as a witness.
Testimony written in a document, meaning his signature as a witness

steps.confusionAlert: The witness was valid when he signed. The problem is only about confirming the signature later in court, after he has become unfit.

phrases.english: Rather, if something is difficult, this is difficult:
One knew testimony for him in a document
phrases.notes: In plain words, he signed as a witness on someone's document.

phrases.english: before he became a robber,
and then he became a robber —

phrases.aramaic: הוּא אֵינוֹ מֵעִיד עַל כְּתַב יָדוֹ,
phrases.english: he may not testify about his own handwriting,
but others may testify.
Now, if he himself is not believed,
are others believed?!
And this is the one that is difficult in monetary law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the בכורה example was rejected in step 5, the גמרא proposes a completely new example.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A witness who became a גזלן after signing cannot confirm his own signature, but others can. This looks illogical.

steps.title: Maybe the signature was already confirmed in court
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the robber example. Maybe the signature had already been confirmed in בית דין before he became a גזלן, so the others are only reporting that fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is so difficult? Maybe it is a case where his handwriting had already been established in court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the robber case and says it is not really difficult.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The others are not confirming the signature fresh. They are only saying that בית דין already confirmed it back when he was still a valid witness. That earlier confirmation still counts, so nothing strange is happening.

phrases.english: What is the difficulty?
Perhaps it is a case where it was already established,
his handwriting, in court!
phrases.notes: This means before he became a robber, back when he was still a valid witness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the example proposed in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the robber ruling is 'difficult.'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case can be read as one where בית דין had already confirmed the signature before he became unfit.

steps.title: A witness who later inherited the property
steps.stepSummary: A new candidate: a witness signed a שטר about a field, and later that field came to him through ירושה. He cannot confirm his signature, but others can.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if there is a difficult ruling, it is this one: someone signed as a witness on a document before the property came to him as an inheritance. He cannot confirm his handwriting, but others can confirm his handwriting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries another example of a 'difficult' ruling: a witness who later inherits the property the שטר is about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the witness inherits, he has a personal stake in the property, so he cannot testify about it. Still, others may confirm his signature, and the same question comes back: why are they believed when he is not?

keyTerms.meaning: To confirm or validate a signature

phrases.english: Rather, if something is difficult, this is difficult:
One knew testimony for him in a document
before it came to him as an inheritance;
phrases.notes: 'It' is the field the document is about. Now the witness himself has a stake in it.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְקַיֵּים כְּתַב יָדוֹ,
phrases.english: he cannot confirm his handwriting,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אֲחֵרִים יְכוֹלִין לְקַיֵּים כְּתַב יָדוֹ.
phrases.english: but others can confirm his handwriting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The robber example failed, so a new example is offered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A witness who later inherits the property cannot confirm his signature, but others can.

steps.title: Same answer: already confirmed in court
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the inheritance case with the same answer: maybe the signature had already been confirmed in בית דין before he inherited.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is so difficult? Maybe here too, it is a case where his handwriting had already been established in court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the inheritance example using the same answer it gave in step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the robber case, this ruling can be read as one where the signature was confirmed while the witness had no stake in the field. The others only report that earlier confirmation, so the ruling is not difficult.

phrases.english: And what is the difficulty?
Perhaps here too,

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהוּחְזַק כְּתַב יָדוֹ בְּבֵית דִּין!
phrases.english: it is a case where his handwriting had been established in court!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer from step 7 to reject the example in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inheritance example as a 'difficult' ruling.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The signature may have been confirmed in בית דין before he inherited.

steps.title: A witness who later became the son-in-law
steps.stepSummary: Another candidate: a witness signed a שטר, then became the person's חתן. As a relative he cannot confirm his own signature, but others can. How can they be believed when he is not?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if there is a difficult ruling, it is this one: someone signed as a witness before he became that person's son-in-law, and then he became his son-in-law. He cannot testify about his handwriting, but others can. He himself is not believed, yet others are believed?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes a third example of a 'difficult' ruling: a witness who later became a relative by marriage of the person in the שטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A relative cannot be a witness, so once he becomes the חתן he cannot confirm his own signature. Yet others may confirm it, and the same question comes back: why are they trusted when he is not?

keyTerms.meaning: A relative, who is not allowed to testify

steps.whatToRemember: All three cases share one pattern: the witness was valid when he signed and became unfit later. The question each time is why others may confirm his signature when he cannot.

phrases.english: Rather, if something is difficult, this is difficult:
One knew testimony about him
before he became his son-in-law,
and then he became his son-in-law —

phrases.aramaic: הוּא אֵינוֹ מֵעִיד עַל כְּתַב יָדוֹ,
phrases.english: he may not testify about his handwriting,
but others may testify.
He is not believed,
yet others are believed?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The inheritance example failed, so a third example is offered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A witness who later became the person's son-in-law cannot confirm his signature, but others can. This seems illogical.

steps.title: The usual rejection does not work for the son-in-law case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks the answer that the signature was already confirmed in בית דין, because רב נחמן allows others to confirm it even without that.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say that here too the signature was already confirmed in court before he became a relative: but רב יוסף בר מניומי said in the name of רב נחמן that others may confirm it even if it was not confirmed in court beforehand!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא expects the same rejection used in Steps 7 and 9 and shows it does not work here. So the חתן case still looks difficult.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the robber and inheritance cases, the גמרא said the signature might have been confirmed in בית דין earlier. Here a ruling of רב נחמן says others can confirm a relative's signature even without earlier confirmation. That removes the escape route, so the question stands: why are others believed when he is not?

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces an expected answer)
His handwriting was confirmed as genuine
But didn't he say? (brings a source against the answer)

phrases.english: And if you would say: here too,

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהוּחְזַק כְּתַב יָדוֹ בְּבֵית דִּין,
phrases.english: it is a case where his handwriting was already confirmed in court,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי
phrases.english: but didn't רב יוסף בר מניומי say
that רב נחמן said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא הוּחְזַק כְּתַב יָדוֹ בְּבֵית דִּין!
phrases.english: even if his handwriting was not confirmed in court!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the חתן candidate from Step 10 against the rejection used in Steps 7 and 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The expected rejection that the signature was confirmed in בית דין before he became a חתן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן rules that others can confirm the signature even without earlier confirmation, so that answer cannot explain this ruling.

steps.title: A relative is disqualified by divine decree, not for lying
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the son-in-law case: a relative is disqualified by a גזירת מלך, so it is not strange that others are believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the difficulty? Perhaps it is a King's decree that he is not believed and others are believed, and it is not because he lies!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the חתן case is not difficult after all. A relative is not disqualified because we suspect him of lying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed the חתן is disqualified because he is not trusted. If others then confirm the same signature, that would seem contradictory. But if the Torah simply rules that relatives cannot testify, then nothing about the facts is being doubted, and others may confirm the signature.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the difficulty? (dismisses a question)
A King's decree: a Torah rule with no stated reason

steps.confusionAlert: A relative is not called a liar. He is fully honest. The Torah simply does not accept his testimony for his relatives.

phrases.english: And what is the difficulty?
Perhaps it is a King's decree,
phrases.notes: The 'King' here means ה׳. It is a Torah rule with no stated reason.

phrases.english: that he is not believed,
and others are believed,
and not because he lies!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי קוּשְׁיָא? דִּלְמָא גְּזֵירַת מֶלֶךְ הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the חתן candidate even though Step 11 blocked the usual rejection.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the son-in-law case as an example of a 'difficult' ruling
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The question wrongly assumed a relative is disqualified because he is suspected of lying.

steps.title: Proof from משה and אהרן
steps.stepSummary: Even משה and אהרן could not testify for their father-in-law, which shows that the disqualification of relatives is a גזירת מלך.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you don't say so, then משה and אהרן for their father-in-law: is it because they are not believed?! Rather, it is a King's decree that they may not testify for them. Here too, it is a King's decree that he may not testify about his handwriting for his father-in-law!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves Step 12. Nobody would suspect משה and אהרן of lying, yet they still could not testify for their relatives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If relatives were disqualified for lying, completely trustworthy people would be allowed to testify. Since even משה and אהרן are disqualified, the rule must be a decree. The same decree covers the חתן confirming his own signature.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you don't say so

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key principle in the laws of עדות: פסול קרובים is a גזירת מלך and does not mean the relatives are dishonest.

phrases.english: For if you don't say so,
משה and אהרן for their father-in-law:
is it because they are not believed?!
Rather, it is a King's decree
that they may not testify for them;
here too, it is a King's decree

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יָעִיד עַל כְּתַב יָדוֹ לְחוֹתְנוֹ!
phrases.english: that he may not testify about his handwriting for his father-in-law!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי, מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן לְחוֹתְנָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the גזירת מלך claim of Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: Relatives are disqualified by a גזירת מלך, not because they are suspected of lying
steps.raayaSupportSource: משה and אהרן could not testify for their father-in-law, even though nobody would suspect them of lying

steps.title: Back to the first case: the פסוק is only a blessing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to its original difficult case and says the פסוק raised against it is only a blessing, not a legal source.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, really it is as we said at first. And as for what was difficult for you, 'In place of your fathers shall be your sons': that is written as a blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting all the other candidates, the גמרא goes back to the first case it called difficult. It answers the earlier challenge from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, someone argued that the פסוק shows a grandson inherits straight from his grandfather. If so, the ruling would not be difficult at all. The גמרא answers that the פסוק is a blessing, not a legal rule, so the original ruling stays difficult.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in truth (returns to an earlier position)
It is written as a blessing

steps.whatToRemember: The robber, inheritance and חתן cases were all rejected. The original case remains the 'difficult' ruling, and the פסוק is read as only a blessing.

phrases.english: Rather, really it is as we said at first,
phrases.notes: This goes back to the first case: a son sold his father's property and died, and his son takes it back.

phrases.english: and what was difficult for you,
'In place of your fathers shall be your sons':
that is written as a blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the חתן case falls in Steps 12-13, the גמרא returns to the original case of Step 1 and answers the פסוק that Step 2 used against it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the פסוק as a blessing rather than a law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to teach that a grandson inherits directly from his grandfather, so the ruling would not be difficult.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק is only a blessing, so the original ruling is still difficult.

steps.title: Can the פסוק really be just a blessing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to question whether the פסוק can be read as only a blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But can you really say that it is written as a blessing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to the answer in Step 14. The full challenge continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said the פסוק is only a blessing. Now the גמרא doubts that reading and prepares to show the פסוק may have legal meaning after all.

keyTerms.meaning: But can you really say? (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But can you really say
that it is written as a blessing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge against the blessing reading of Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'תחת אבותיך יהיו בניך' is only a blessing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The challenge is only being set up here. The reason the blessing reading fails comes in the continuation.
